A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.
Since M4b the terms of the vendored Plaits (`vendor/plaits/`, read only from
its checksum-verified files) are public like the SDK's, the check says how
many emulator terms that takes off, and `vendor/plaits/` itself is not
scanned, except its `SOURCE.md`, which we write (R-SEP-1).

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
  `records` environment's deploy key.
- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
  SBOM.

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
  with GitHub's key instead.
- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.

What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):

- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
  role).
- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
  pushes; no bypass.
- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
  bypass.

Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
off).

Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
GitHub API:

| What | ID or fingerprint |
|------|-------------------|
| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |

deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new
public key, delete the old key.

   ```

   `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`, then
   `git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.

   tag as **Verified**.

  `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` and `SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98`.
  Files that can't carry one are covered in `REUSE.toml`.
- Vendored files keep their own licences (`vendor/*/LICENSE`, `NOTICE`).
- CI runs `reuse lint` and fails on any gap (C-REUSE).
- Never commit the toolchain or anything containing it (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md).
- Nothing secret ever goes in: no keys, tokens or private notes. The
  repository is public and history is never rewritten.

## Privacy

The repository is public. No committed file, commit message or pull request
text names the owner's username, real name, e-mail address, hostname or
local folder names, or a full local path: write paths relative to the
repository, or as `~/...` with the top folder shown as `<top>`. Anyone who
finds such a term in the repository tells the owner instead of repeating it.

  gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` (one per line, `#` comments,
  matched ignoring case) and in the repository secret `PRIVATE_TERMS`, which
  CI passes to the check.

  tracked file and every commit message, and the pre-commit and commit-msg

firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the

## A: a table-less ALU word that heads a pair runs as one

- **Encoding**: the 4-byte ALU forms `decode_alu4` reads when no table class fits (`alu4_craw` in
  `decode_any`), with byte 1 `f0` / `f1`, the dual-issue pair head, which `decode_alu4` reads as
  `e0` / `e1`. Rainbow's `94 f1 80 0c`, `r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #`, followed by `[sp+16] = r0`.
- **The bug**: the fallback entry's syntax has no trailing `#`, so the core runs the word unpaired:
  its result is written at once, and the pair's second half sees the new value. Every other `f0` /
  `f1` form in the table is a pair head (upstream's own `df06519` row for `94 f1 .3` among them),
  and so is this one. The fork found it on Rainbow, whose store saved the new r0, not the old. (By
  the encoding rule and the firmware's code, not checked on a chip.)
- **Reproduction** (a raw image, 32 bytes, at 0x02000000):

  ```
  c0 ff 55 00 00 00   r0 = 0x55
  c8 ff 00 01 00 00   r8 = 0x100
  cc ff 03 00 00 00   r12 = 3
  c4 ff 20 00 c0 01   r4 = 0x01C00020
  94 f1 80 0c         r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #     (the pair's head)
  c0 60               [r4+0] = r0                (its second half: sees r0 = 0x55)
  f7 9f               goto itself
  ```

  As hex: `c0ff55000000c8ff00010000ccff03000000c4ff2000c00194f1800cc060f79f`. With fwtest:
  `tools/fwtest run IMAGE --ms 1 --ram 0x01c00020:4@end`. Expected: the word at 0x01C00020 is
  `0x00000055`, and r0 ends `0x108`. Upstream `43ed558`, and so fwtest today, stores `0x00000108`.
  Checked here on both trees, with a small runner over `raw_boot`, a step at a time and through
  `run_fast` with the JIT: upstream stores 0x108, the patched tree 0x55; both end with r0 = 0x108.
  (Not yet run on fwtest itself: the command line is from small-beeps' SR-7 request.)

  arm (no table class and no earlier raw decoder took them), and of those only the ones whose
  byte 1 is `f0` or `f1`. Those are the pair-head twins of these `decode_alu4` families (byte 0,
  byte 1; R is a register, # an immediate):

  | Bytes | Form |
  |---|---|
  | `b4 f0` | `R = R + R #`, `R = R - R #` (sub-op 0, 2) |
  | `90 f1` | `R = R \| R #`, `R = R ^ R #`, `R = R & R #` |
  | `94 f1` | `R = R \| (1 << R) #`, `^`, `&`, `& ~` (Rainbow's `94 f1 80 0c`: `\|`) |
  | `c8 f1` | `R = R << R #`, `>>`, `>>>` (shift by a register) |
  | `f0 f1` | `R = R * R #` |
  | `Xe f0`, `Xf f0`, `Xa f0` | `R = R + #i #`, `R = R - #i #`, `R = #i - R #` (byte 0's high nibble e, f, a) |
  | `X0`..`X3 f1` | `R = R + #i #` (14-bit) |
  | `X4`..`X7 f1`, `Xe f1` | `R = R \| #i #`, `^`, `&`, `& ~`, `*` |

  Every other word decodes as before: the table's rows and the other raw decoders are untouched,
  and a word with byte 1 `e0`/`e1` (not a pair head) still gets `ALU4_CRAW`. None of the memory

  meet only in `decode_any`, A in the `decode_alu4` arm and the `ALU4_PAIR_CRAW` entry beside
  `ALU4_CRAW`, so a hunk of one may need its context refreshed after the other lands.
- **Test**: `alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head` (fm1-core) runs the word alone: a pair pending, r0 held

- **The fingerprint run** (79 Hub firmwares, 5 s at 240 MHz): only Rainbow changes, back to what it

## D: blocks over RAM checked by the write count on every build (speed only)

A block built from RAM code is checked before every entry. Upstream's wasm build skips the byte
compare while the bus's count of writes to code words is the one the block was last found current
at; native builds compared the bytes every time. Every store to a code word is counted (the
interpreter's through the bus; both native JITs, AArch64 and x86-64, send inline stores to a
flagged word to the bus; bulk loads count themselves), so the shortcut is now every build's. The
test, `ram_block_sees_patched_code` (fm1-soc), re-enters a RAM block after a store patched its
immediate, interpreted and with the JIT, and fails if the RAM stops counting code-word writes.
When the fork first made it (`9ea2e84`, on upstream `7856393`), interpreted as on iOS, melodee ran
41% faster with it, bubba 11%, M-VAVE's own 4%; not measured again on `43ed558`. fwtest doesn't
need it.

> **fm1-core: `alu4_craw` words with byte 1 f0/f1 run unpaired**
>
> A 4-byte ALU word that no table class fits is decoded by `decode_alu4` (`decode_any`'s

306	## D: blocks over RAM checked by the write count on every build (speed only)
307	
308	A block built from RAM code is checked before every entry. Upstream's wasm build skips the byte
309	compare while the bus's count of writes to code words is the one the block was last found current

311	interpreter's through the bus; both native JITs, AArch64 and x86-64, send inline stores to a
312	flagged word to the bus; bulk loads count themselves), so the shortcut is now every build's. The

316	41% faster with it, bubba 11%, M-VAVE's own 4%; not measured again on `43ed558`. fwtest doesn't
317	need it.

490	+    }

495	+    /// A raw image's sizes: 1 byte to 1 MiB less 16 KiB; past it, and in its last word, the
496	+    /// erased chip.

501	+        assert!(e.contains("1032193 bytes") && e.contains("1032192"), "{e}");

512	+        assert_eq!(soc.read32(XIP_BASE + 0x1000), 0xffff_ffff, "past the image: the erased chip");

515	     /// A block over RAM re-entered after a store patched its code runs the new code, interpreted
516	     /// and with the JIT (blocks over RAM skip their byte compare while the bus's count of
517	     /// code-word writes is unchanged, so every store to a code word must be counted).
518	```

520	## The sync's fingerprint run
521	
522	The 79 Hub firmwares (5 s at 240 MHz, a chord at 3 s; the fingerprint is audio, screen and the
523	CPU's end state), before the sync (the fork on upstream `7856393`) and after (`43ed558` with A to
524	E): no firmware halts, and no firmware's audio changes. 22 fingerprints change, all from upstream
525	(each firmware fingerprinted at every upstream merge, and inside PR #28 at every commit):
526	
527	| Upstream commit | Firmwares | What changes |
528	|---|---|---|
529	| `b80fa6b` (the compiler's DSP builtins; `<<<` saturates, a shift count of 0 is 32) | etch, felucca8, fmini, frodhes, gammawave, minitone, mycelium, noizdemons, skiff, sloop, sloopdx, tuna, unholy, winampfm | CPU end state; mycelium's screen |
530	| `af1f590` (ALNK0's receive channel pends with each block; more DSP forms) | cs1, felucca-salt, fimba (also below), niagara | CPU end state |
531	| both | nmsfm, orbit | CPU end state; nmsfm's screen |
532	| `7d15144` (P33 modelled) and `0583b22` (`64bed7f`'s decodes, in place of the fork's) | beetle, mc1 | CPU end state |
533	
534	beetle, fimba and mc1 also change at the first step, bare upstream `7856393` without the fork's
535	changes (its forms and P33; mc1 halts there, as it did before the fork's `64 f0` decode), so part of
536	their change is upstream's versions standing in for the fork's. Rainbow changes at that step too,
537	and A puts it back.
538	
539	The 4 s real-time boot run: all 79 boot, none halts, every screen draws. Speed is as before,
540	the two builds run alternately: interpreted, as on iOS, 0.3% faster over the 12 firmwares of
541	`crates/fm1-ios/perf/bench.sh` (each within 3%); with the Mac's JIT, within 5% on eight. small-beeps `dc82c85` runs as before: its screens,
542	every key sounding and lighting its LED, MASTER scaling the level, no halt.
543	
544	## Upstream bug reports (to file)
545	
546	### 1. A table-less ALU pair head runs unpaired: `94 f1 80 0c` stores the new value
547	
548	> **fm1-core: `alu4_craw` words with byte 1 f0/f1 run unpaired**
549	>
550	> A 4-byte ALU word that no table class fits is decoded by `decode_alu4` (`decode_any`'s
551	> `Err(_) if decode_alu4(...)` arm, entry `ALU4_CRAW`). `decode_alu4` reads byte 1 `f0`/`f1` as
552	> `e0`/`e1`, but `ALU4_CRAW`'s syntax has no trailing `#`, so the word doesn't head a pair: its
553	> result is written at once and the pair's second half sees it. Rainbow (FM-1 Firmware Hub) has
554	> `94 f1 80 0c` (`r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #`) then `[sp+16] = r0`, and stores the new r0.
555	>
556	> Reproduction, a raw image at 0x02000000 (hex):
557	> `c0ff55000000c8ff00010000ccff03000000c4ff2000c00194f1800cc060f79f` (r0 = 0x55, r8 = 0x100,
558	> r12 = 3, r4 = 0x01C00020, the pair head, `[r4+0] = r0`, a jump to itself). The word at
559	> 0x01C00020 should be 0x55; it is 0x108.
560	>
561	> Fix: an `ALU4_PAIR_CRAW` entry, the same with `#` at the end of its syntax, for words whose byte
562	> 1 is f0/f1; a test, `alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head`. (The patch: 0003 above.)
563	
564	### 2. SPI1's CON keeps bits once written
565	
566	small-beeps' report covers it: `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-spi1-con.md` in
567	[small-beeps](https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps). File that one (it's the owner's to file);
568	this fork's test, `spi1_con_write_replaces` (B above), can go with it.
569	
570	### 3. The crates need Rust 1.95, unsaid
571	
572	> **fm1-core needs Rust 1.95 (`if let` match guards) but the workspace doesn't say so**
573	>
574	> `decode_any` uses `None if let Some(entry) = ...` guards (`sreg_move_raw`, `pre_table_raw`),
575	> stable from Rust 1.95; on 1.94 the build fails with E0658. Either set `rust-version = "1.95"` in
576	> the workspace manifest, or write the two arms as a nested match (the same order: the
577	> special-register moves, then the DSP forms, then the table).
578	
579	### Suggestions, not bugs
580	
581	C and D above as pull requests, if upstream wants the speed: neither changes what any address or
582	block does, and each has its test.

# Emulator patches: this fork against upstream and small-beeps' fwtest

The emulator core (crates/fm1-isa, fm1-core, fm1-soc) here is upstream
[fm1-emu](https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu) at `43ed558`, the commit small-beeps' `fwtest`
vendors (small-beeps `24935c0`, `vendor/emulator/UPSTREAM.md`), with a few changes of this fork's
on top, each its own commit with a test (branch `upstream-sync`). This file lists them for two
readers:

- **small-beeps' harness**: each patch below is a unified diff against small-beeps' vendored tree
  (upstream `43ed558` with its `0001` and `0002` applied), in its `vendor/emulator/patches/` form,
  numbered to follow `0002`. All four apply in order with `git apply`, and the crates' tests pass
  after each, on Rust 1.95 as upstream needs.
- **upstream**: the bug reports at the end, ready to file.

| | What | Upstream `43ed558` | fwtest (small-beeps `24935c0`) | Here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | A table-less ALU word that heads a pair runs as one (`94 f1 80 0c`) | Bug | Bug | `681701d`, test `alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head` |
| B | A write to SPI1's CON replaces it | Bug | Fixed (its `0002`) | `d9f0dda`, test `spi1_con_write_replaces` |
| C | Register accesses skip the memories | Not there (speed only) | Not needed | `ae32314`, test `region_is_what_it_was` |
| D | Blocks over RAM checked by the write count on every build | wasm only (speed only) | Not needed | `de669c1`, test `ram_block_sees_patched_code` |
| E | Boot a raw image | Not there | Its own (in `harness/`) | `446d11c`, test `raw_image_sizes` |

Only A changes what a firmware does in fwtest today. C and D change nothing but speed (their tests
show it), and E is the app's version of what fwtest already does; they're here so the two trees can
be compared, and so the patches stack as the app's do.

Also on the branch, not a patch for anyone: `cb85332` rewrites two `if let` match guards in
`decode_any` as a nested match, so the crates build on Rust 1.94 (this Mac's, and the one the iOS
build's PGO profile was made with); no change in what decodes.

## What the fork had that upstream now does itself

Before the sync the fork carried its own versions of these. Upstream `43ed558` has them, so they
were dropped; the fork's own tests for them pass on upstream's code unchanged.

| The fork's | Encoding | Upstream's |
|---|---|---|
| `4fd73b9`: `[R+#i] &= ~R` at any offset (CutAdor, Mutable, ObervaVe, ShineOn) | `64 e8 .3` | `ebe397a` (and-not's four-bit register field) |
| `4fd73b9`: `R = R & ~(1 << R)`, the pair head too (Duell, EMB) | `94 e1/f1 .3` | `df06519`, `302cf38` |
| `4fd73b9`: the special-register moves as a pair head (386DX, CTL, MC-1) | `64 f0 00 XY` | `64bed7f` |
| `4fd73b9`: bit tests jumping forward (Kawa) | `60 ff` / `61 ff` | `64bed7f` |
| `fa41abf`: P33's registers read back (Melodee boots) | P33_CON / P33_DAT, 0x13E08 / 0x13E0C | `ab0f422` (p33.rs) |

The fifth part of `4fd73b9`, the pair head in the table-less ALU fallback, upstream doesn't have:
that's A.

## A: a table-less ALU word that heads a pair runs as one

- **Encoding**: the 4-byte ALU forms `decode_alu4` reads when no table class fits (`alu4_craw` in
  `decode_any`), with byte 1 `f0` / `f1`, the dual-issue pair head, which `decode_alu4` reads as
  `e0` / `e1`. Rainbow's `94 f1 80 0c`, `r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #`, followed by `[sp+16] = r0`.
- **The bug**: the fallback entry's syntax has no trailing `#`, so the core runs the word unpaired:
  its result is written at once, and the pair's second half sees the new value. Every other `f0` /
  `f1` form in the table is a pair head (upstream's own `df06519` row for `94 f1 .3` among them),
  and so is this one. The fork found it on Rainbow, whose store saved the new r0, not the old. (By
  the encoding rule and the firmware's code, not checked on a chip.)
- **Reproduction** (a raw image, 32 bytes, at 0x02000000):

  ```
  c0 ff 55 00 00 00   r0 = 0x55
  c8 ff 00 01 00 00   r8 = 0x100
  cc ff 03 00 00 00   r12 = 3
  c4 ff 20 00 c0 01   r4 = 0x01C00020
  94 f1 80 0c         r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #     (the pair's head)
  c0 60               [r4+0] = r0                (its second half: sees r0 = 0x55)
  f7 9f               goto itself
  ```

  As hex: `c0ff55000000c8ff00010000ccff03000000c4ff2000c00194f1800cc060f79f`. With fwtest:
  `tools/fwtest run IMAGE --ms 1 --ram 0x01c00020:4@end`. Expected: the word at 0x01C00020 is
  `0x00000055`, and r0 ends `0x108`. Upstream `43ed558`, and so fwtest today, stores `0x00000108`.
  Checked here on both trees, with a small runner over `raw_boot`, a step at a time and through
  `run_fast` with the JIT: upstream stores 0x108, the patched tree 0x55; both end with r0 = 0x108.
  (Not yet run on fwtest itself: the command line is from small-beeps' SR-7 request.)
- **Exactly what it touches**: only words that reach `decode_any`'s `Err(_) if decode_alu4(...)`
  arm (no table class and no earlier raw decoder took them), and of those only the ones whose
  byte 1 is `f0` or `f1`. Those are the pair-head twins of these `decode_alu4` families (byte 0,
  byte 1; R is a register, # an immediate):

  | Bytes | Form |
  |---|---|
  | `b4 f0` | `R = R + R #`, `R = R - R #` (sub-op 0, 2) |
  | `90 f1` | `R = R \| R #`, `R = R ^ R #`, `R = R & R #` |
  | `94 f1` | `R = R \| (1 << R) #`, `^`, `&`, `& ~` (Rainbow's `94 f1 80 0c`: `\|`) |
  | `c8 f1` | `R = R << R #`, `>>`, `>>>` (shift by a register) |
  | `f0 f1` | `R = R * R #` |
  | `Xe f0`, `Xf f0`, `Xa f0` | `R = R + #i #`, `R = R - #i #`, `R = #i - R #` (byte 0's high nibble e, f, a) |
  | `X0`..`X3 f1` | `R = R + #i #` (14-bit) |
  | `X4`..`X7 f1`, `Xe f1` | `R = R \| #i #`, `^`, `&`, `& ~`, `*` |

  Every other word decodes as before: the table's rows and the other raw decoders are untouched,
  and a word with byte 1 `e0`/`e1` (not a pair head) still gets `ALU4_CRAW`. None of the memory
  forms `decode_alu4` knows (byte 1 `e8`, `eb`, `ef`) changes. **SR-7** (`{r3, r0} = [-r4]`,
  `44 eb 09 00`, and its block-move / two-register load kin) has byte 1 `eb`, a load family the
  fallback arm doesn't take (fwtest faults on it), so the two patches touch no common form; they
  meet only in `decode_any`, A in the `decode_alu4` arm and the `ALU4_PAIR_CRAW` entry beside
  `ALU4_CRAW`, so a hunk of one may need its context refreshed after the other lands.
- **Test**: `alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head` (fm1-core) runs the word alone: a pair pending, r0 held
  back, 0x108 after. It fails without the patch.
- **The fingerprint run** (79 Hub firmwares, 5 s at 240 MHz): only Rainbow changes, back to what it
  was before the sync.

`0003-alu4-fallback-pair-head.patch`:

```diff
The 4-byte ALU forms no table class fits (alu4_craw) ran unpaired even when
byte 1 is f0 / f1, the dual-issue pair head: in Rainbow's `94 f1 80 0c`
`r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #` then `[sp+16] = r0`, the store saw the new r0. Such
words now decode as a pair head (ALU4_PAIR_CRAW, syntax ending in `#`).
Test alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head fails without it.

+        let mut mem = vec![0u8; 0x100];

```

## B: a write to SPI1's CON replaces it

fwtest has this (`0002-spi1-con-writes-replace.patch`, small-beeps session SR-3), and small-beeps'
`harness/upstream/fm1-emu-spi1-con.md` is its report to upstream; the fork's change is the same
code. A write to 0x11D00 was OR-ed into the stored value, so once any write set bit 13 (the
transfer-done interrupt enable), every later SPI1 transfer raised IRQ 16. The fork's test,
`spi1_con_write_replaces` (fm1-soc): CON written 0x2001 then 0x0001, a byte through BUF (0x11D08),
then no IRQ 16 pending and CON reading 0x0001 (bit 15, transfer done, masked); with bit 13 set
again, the same transfer raises it. small-beeps' own test is its harness's
`spi1_interrupt_follows_con_bit_13`. No patch here: fwtest's `0002` is it.

## C: register accesses skip the memories (speed only)

`Soc::region` tried the RAM, XIP, overlay and SRAM2 ranges before the peripherals'. Everything
below 16 MB is a peripheral (all but the interrupt controller's), so `region` now sends those
addresses to `region_low` first. No address reaches anything different: `region_is_what_it_was`
compares every address below 0x04200000, and a sweep above, with upstream's function, for both
boards and both XIP-flash settings. (Upstream's P33 region, `ab0f422`, covers what the fork's
version of this also did for P33.) fwtest doesn't need it.

## D: blocks over RAM checked by the write count on every build (speed only)

A block built from RAM code is checked before every entry. Upstream's wasm build skips the byte
compare while the bus's count of writes to code words is the one the block was last found current
at; native builds compared the bytes every time. Every store to a code word is counted (the
interpreter's through the bus; both native JITs, AArch64 and x86-64, send inline stores to a
flagged word to the bus; bulk loads count themselves), so the shortcut is now every build's. The
test, `ram_block_sees_patched_code` (fm1-soc), re-enters a RAM block after a store patched its
immediate, interpreted and with the JIT, and fails if the RAM stops counting code-word writes.

41% faster with it, bubba 11%, M-VAVE's own 4%; not measured again on `43ed558`. fwtest doesn't
need it.

The 79 Hub firmwares (5 s at 240 MHz, a chord at 3 s; the fingerprint is audio, screen and the
CPU's end state), before the sync (the fork on upstream `7856393`) and after (`43ed558` with A to
E): no firmware halts, and no firmware's audio changes. 22 fingerprints change, all from upstream
(each firmware fingerprinted at every upstream merge, and inside PR #28 at every commit):

| Upstream commit | Firmwares | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `b80fa6b` (the compiler's DSP builtins; `<<<` saturates, a shift count of 0 is 32) | etch, felucca8, fmini, frodhes, gammawave, minitone, mycelium, noizdemons, skiff, sloop, sloopdx, tuna, unholy, winampfm | CPU end state; mycelium's screen |
| `af1f590` (ALNK0's receive channel pends with each block; more DSP forms) | cs1, felucca-salt, fimba (also below), niagara | CPU end state |
| both | nmsfm, orbit | CPU end state; nmsfm's screen |
| `7d15144` (P33 modelled) and `0583b22` (`64bed7f`'s decodes, in place of the fork's) | beetle, mc1 | CPU end state |

changes (its forms and P33; mc1 halts there, as it did before the fork's `64 f0` decode), so part of

and A puts it back.

the two builds run alternately: interpreted, as on iOS, 0.3% faster over the 12 firmwares of

every key sounding and lighting its LED, MASTER scaling the level, no halt.

## Upstream bug reports (to file)

### 1. A table-less ALU pair head runs unpaired: `94 f1 80 0c` stores the new value

> **fm1-core: `alu4_craw` words with byte 1 f0/f1 run unpaired**
>
> A 4-byte ALU word that no table class fits is decoded by `decode_alu4` (`decode_any`'s
> `Err(_) if decode_alu4(...)` arm, entry `ALU4_CRAW`). `decode_alu4` reads byte 1 `f0`/`f1` as
> `e0`/`e1`, but `ALU4_CRAW`'s syntax has no trailing `#`, so the word doesn't head a pair: its
> result is written at once and the pair's second half sees it. Rainbow (FM-1 Firmware Hub) has
> `94 f1 80 0c` (`r0 = r8 | (1 << r12) #`) then `[sp+16] = r0`, and stores the new r0.
>
> Reproduction, a raw image at 0x02000000 (hex):
> `c0ff55000000c8ff00010000ccff03000000c4ff2000c00194f1800cc060f79f` (r0 = 0x55, r8 = 0x100,
> r12 = 3, r4 = 0x01C00020, the pair head, `[r4+0] = r0`, a jump to itself). The word at
> 0x01C00020 should be 0x55; it is 0x108.
>
> Fix: an `ALU4_PAIR_CRAW` entry, the same with `#` at the end of its syntax, for words whose byte
> 1 is f0/f1; a test, `alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head`. (The patch: 0003 above.)

### 2. SPI1's CON keeps bits once written

small-beeps' report covers it: `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-spi1-con.md` in
[small-beeps](https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps). File that one (it's the owner's to file);
this fork's test, `spi1_con_write_replaces` (B above), can go with it.

### 3. The crates need Rust 1.95, unsaid

> **fm1-core needs Rust 1.95 (`if let` match guards) but the workspace doesn't say so**
>
> `decode_any` uses `None if let Some(entry) = ...` guards (`sreg_move_raw`, `pre_table_raw`),
> stable from Rust 1.95; on 1.94 the build fails with E0658. Either set `rust-version = "1.95"` in
> the workspace manifest, or write the two arms as a nested match (the same order: the
> special-register moves, then the DSP forms, then the table).

C and D above as pull requests, if upstream wants the speed: neither changes what any address or
block does, and each has its test.

## Patches

Applied in file-name order by the fetch script, after checkout:

- `patches/0001-workspace-members.patch`: the three crates take their
  version, edition and licence from the workspace manifest, which upstream
  lists with seven members. The patch keeps the manifest and lists only the
  three vendored crates, so they build as path dependencies of `harness/`.
  No code is changed.
- `patches/0002-spi1-con-writes-replace.patch` (session SR-3, 2026-10-23,
  chosen by the owner): `crates/fm1-soc/src/lib.rs`, SPI1's `CON` write
  (0x11D00). Upstream merged each written value into the stored one, so a
  bit once written 1 could never be cleared, and after any write with bit
  13 every SPI1 transfer raised IRQ 16. With the patch a write replaces
  `CON` (bit 14 stays a strobe that clears the pending flag, not stored).
  The harness test `spi1_interrupt_follows_con_bit_13` fails without it.
  To be reported upstream by the owner from
  `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-spi1-con.md`; drop the patch when the pinned commit has the fix.
- `patches/0003-block-moves-below-the-base.patch` (session SR-7,
  2026-10-24, asked for by the firmware side's SR-7):
  `crates/fm1-core/src/lib.rs`, the block moves with a register base
  (`xm eb <mask>`, m < 8). Upstream ran only the four ascending modes,
  chosen by the table's syntax; `{..} = [-rN]`, `[-rN] = {..}` and the
  `[--rN]` forms ended the run as "an instruction the emulator does not
  implement", and the vendor compiler emits the first two on its own. With
  the patch the family is chosen on its raw bits and one helper runs all
  eight modes, for the interpreter and the fast path; the ascending modes
  behave as before. Behaviour from the vendor compiler's own code
  (`harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md`, docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-66).
  The harness tests `block_moves_every_mode`,
  `block_move_below_the_base_sr7` and `block_moves_from_the_compiler` fail
  without it. To be reported upstream by the owner from that file; drop the
  patch when the pinned commit has the fix.

## Not used

The harness never calls the crates' update-package and stock-boot paths
(`fwsc`, `stock_from_package`, `stock_boot`, `write_boot_info`); they are
vendored only because the crate is kept whole. C-HARNESS-SCOPE checks
that `harness/src` names none of them.
Block moves with a register base, all eight modes: `xm eb <mask>` with
m < 8 (base in bits 0-3, register mask in bits 16-31). Mode bit 4 writes
the base back, bit 5 stores, bit 6 places the block just below the base.
Upstream ran only the four ascending modes (`[rN+]`, `[rN++]`), keyed on
the table's syntax; the descending ones (`{..} = [-rN]`, `[-rN] = {..}`,
`[--rN]` both ways) ended the run as "an instruction the emulator does not
implement". The vendor compiler emits `{rA, rB} = [-rN]` and
`[-rN] = {rA, rB}` on its own (seen in our firmware's struct copies), so
an ordinary C build could not run.

Behaviour, from the vendor compiler's own output (which uses these forms
in code whose meaning is known; harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md):
the lowest-numbered register takes the lowest address; `[-rN]` covers the
words from rN - 4n to rN - 4; the forms without `++`/`--` leave the base as
it was; every address comes from the original base, so a base that is
also in a loaded list ends with its loaded word. The write-back modes are
taken by analogy (the compiler was not seen to emit them): `[--rN]` leaves
rN - 4n in the base, `[rN++]` rN + 4n, as upstream already did.

Decoded from the raw bits, as the other raw-decoded families are; one
helper serves the interpreter and the fast path. Session SR-7, 2026-10-24.

- Provenance: PROVENANCE.md P-7. Exposure: docs/EXPOSURE.md (session M0b).

## Patches

Applied in file-name order by the fetch script, after checkout:

- `patches/0001-workspace-members.patch`: the three crates take their
  version, edition and licence from the workspace manifest, which upstream
  lists with seven members. The patch keeps the manifest and lists only the
  three vendored crates, so they build as path dependencies of `harness/`.
  No code is changed.
- `patches/0002-spi1-con-writes-replace.patch` (session SR-3, 2026-10-23,
  chosen by the owner): `crates/fm1-soc/src/lib.rs`, SPI1's `CON` write
  (0x11D00). Upstream merged each written value into the stored one, so a
  bit once written 1 could never be cleared, and after any write with bit
  13 every SPI1 transfer raised IRQ 16. With the patch a write replaces
  `CON` (bit 14 stays a strobe that clears the pending flag, not stored).
  The harness test `spi1_interrupt_follows_con_bit_13` fails without it.
  To be reported upstream by the owner from
  `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-spi1-con.md`; drop the patch when the pinned commit has the fix.
- `patches/0003-block-moves-below-the-base.patch` (session SR-7,
  2026-10-24, asked for by the firmware side's SR-7):
  `crates/fm1-core/src/lib.rs`, the block moves with a register base
  (`xm eb <mask>`, m < 8). Upstream ran only the four ascending modes,
  chosen by the table's syntax; `{..} = [-rN]`, `[-rN] = {..}` and the
  `[--rN]` forms ended the run as "an instruction the emulator does not
  implement", and the vendor compiler emits the first two on its own. With
  the patch the family is chosen on its raw bits and one helper runs all
  eight modes, for the interpreter and the fast path; the ascending modes
  behave as before. Behaviour from the vendor compiler's own code
  (`harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md`, docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-66).
  The harness tests `block_moves_every_mode`,
  `block_move_below_the_base_sr7` and `block_moves_from_the_compiler` fail
  without it. To be reported upstream by the owner from that file; drop the
  patch when the pinned commit has the fix.

## Not used

The harness never calls the crates' update-package and stock-boot paths
(`fwsc`, `stock_from_package`, `stock_boot`, `write_boot_info`); they are
vendored only because the crate is kept whole. C-HARNESS-SCOPE checks
that `harness/src` names none of them.
Block moves with a register base, all eight modes: `xm eb <mask>` with
m < 8 (base in bits 0-3, register mask in bits 16-31). Mode bit 4 writes
the base back, bit 5 stores, bit 6 places the block just below the base.
Upstream ran only the four ascending modes (`[rN+]`, `[rN++]`), keyed on
the table's syntax; the descending ones (`{..} = [-rN]`, `[-rN] = {..}`,
`[--rN]` both ways) ended the run as "an instruction the emulator does not
implement". The vendor compiler emits `{rA, rB} = [-rN]` and
`[-rN] = {rA, rB}` on its own (seen in our firmware's struct copies), so
an ordinary C build could not run.

Behaviour, from the vendor compiler's own output (which uses these forms
in code whose meaning is known; harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md):
the lowest-numbered register takes the lowest address; `[-rN]` covers the
words from rN - 4n to rN - 4; the forms without `++`/`--` leave the base as
it was; every address comes from the original base, so a base that is
also in a loaded list ends with its loaded word. The write-back modes are
taken by analogy (the compiler was not seen to emit them): `[--rN]` leaves
rN - 4n in the base, `[rN++]` rN + 4n, as upstream already did.

Decoded from the raw bits, as the other raw-decoded families are; one
helper serves the interpreter and the fast path. Session SR-7, 2026-10-24.

# Upstream report: two instruction forms that don't decode

For the owner to file with `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` and, if wanted, to
apply in the F-Emulator app. Spec side only; not filed by a session. Found
in session SR-7 (2026-10-24) against commit
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`, after the block-move fix
(`fm1-emu-block-moves.md`). Not patched in our copy: fwtest 0.3.0 still
stops on both, and docs/HARNESS.md ("Instructions") lists them as known
gaps.

How they were found: a corpus of C and C++ (our firmware, Mutable
Instruments' Plaits, generated C) built with the vendor compiler (clang
4.0.1 pi32v2, `-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`, `-Os` and `-O2`); each of the 660
forms in its assembly output, with every register slot set in turn to r0
to r15 and every number to a spread of values, assembled by the vendor
assembler and run on its own. 34 437 distinct encodings; these two forms
are the only ones that stop the run. Both fail in `decode_any`
(`decode_info` returns `None`): "an instruction the emulated CPU cannot
decode".

## 1. Rotate by a register: `rD = rS <> rT`

| Instruction | Bytes |
|-------------|-------|
| `r0 = r0 <> r1` | `cc e1 00 01` |
| `r5 = r9 <> r2` | `cc e1 90 52` |
| `r15 = r3 <> r14` | `cc e1 30 fe` |

None decodes, for any registers. The rotate by a constant,

emits the register form for any rotate by a variable amount:
`(x << s) | (x >> (32 - s))` becomes `r1 = 0x20 - r1; r0 = r0 <> r1`, and
`(x >> 7) | (x << 25)` becomes `r0 = r0 <> 7`. So `<>` rotates right, by
the register's amount; what it does with amounts of 32 or more, the
compiler's code doesn't show.

## 2. 4-byte register-list push and pop, lowest register above r0

`[--sp] = {list}` is `d8 e8 <mask>` and `{list} = [sp++]` is
`d4 e8 <mask>` (no `rets`, no `pc`; mask bit k: rk). They decode only
when the list starts at r0:

`d1 e8` and `d5 e8` mask families that already have raw decoders
(`RETS_PUSH_MASK_CRAW`, `RETS_POP_MASK_CRAW`, `PC_POP_MASK_CRAW`). The
compiler was not seen to emit the failing lists: its interrupt handlers
save a list from r0 (`[--sp] = {r1, r0}`, `{r7-r0} = [sp++]`). Hand-written
assembly can. A raw decoder for `d8 e8` and `d4 e8` like those three would
cover every mask.

bytes above, then a halt. The run stops at the start of that code,

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Vendors three crates of the public emulator upstream, at a pinned commit,
# into vendor/emulator/, applies the patches in vendor/emulator/patches/, and
# checks every file against vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS, whose own SHA-256 is
# the tree hash below (PROVENANCE P-7). Spec side only: vendor/emulator/ is
# left out of clean folders, and --fetch refuses to run in one.
#
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --verify   check the committed files (default,
#                                      offline; SKIP when vendor/emulator/
#                                      isn't on disk, as in a clean folder)
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --fetch    re-download them from the pinned commit,
#                                      apply the patches, then verify
#
# The fetch is a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout of exactly the paths
# in UPSTREAM_PATHS, so nothing else in that repository reaches the disk.
# To move to another commit: change UPSTREAM_COMMIT, run --fetch in a spec
# folder, rewrite SHA256SUMS (--sums), update TREE_SHA256 and UPSTREAM.md,
# and log it in PROVENANCE.md, all in one pull request.
set -eu

UPSTREAM_URL=https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu.git
UPSTREAM_COMMIT=43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f
UPSTREAM_PATHS="
/LICENSE
/Cargo.toml
/crates/fm1-isa/
/crates/fm1-core/
/crates/fm1-soc/
"
# SHA-256 of vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS: one hash for the whole tree.
TREE_SHA256=0553473ab8b76fe289c0c4c7609ed3ade622a5f4510b185b099cfdcb7bfd4a29

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
DEST="$ROOT/vendor/emulator"
SUMS="$DEST/SHA256SUMS"
# Ours, not upstream's: not listed in SHA256SUMS.
OURS="SHA256SUMS UPSTREAM.md"

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

listed_files() {
    (cd "$DEST" && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort) | while read -r f; do
        case " $OURS " in *" $f "*) continue ;; esac
        printf '%s\n' "$f"
    done
}

verify() {
    if [ ! -d "$DEST" ]; then
        echo "SKIP: vendor/emulator/ is not on disk (a clean folder leaves it out)"
        return 0
    fi
    status=0
    got=$(sha256 "$SUMS")
    if [ "$got" = "$TREE_SHA256" ]; then echo "OK      SHA256SUMS (tree hash $TREE_SHA256)"
    else echo "CHANGED SHA256SUMS ($got, want $TREE_SHA256)"; status=1; fi
    while read -r want path; do
        [ -n "$want" ] || continue
        if [ ! -f "$DEST/$path" ]; then
            echo "MISSING $path"; status=1; continue
        fi
        [ "$(sha256 "$DEST/$path")" = "$want" ] || { echo "CHANGED $path"; status=1; }
    done < "$SUMS"
    for f in $(listed_files); do
        if ! awk -v p="$f" '$2 == p { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$SUMS"; then
            echo "UNLISTED $f"; status=1
        fi
    done
    n=$(grep -c . "$SUMS")
    if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then echo "$n emulator files match commit $UPSTREAM_COMMIT plus patches"; fi
    return $status
}

sums() {
    (cd "$DEST" && for f in $(listed_files); do printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256 "$f")" "$f"; done) > "$SUMS"
    echo "wrote SHA256SUMS: tree hash $(sha256 "$SUMS")"
}

refuse_in_clean_folder() {
    role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$role" = clean ] || git -C "$ROOT" sparse-checkout list 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^!/vendor/emulator/'; then
        echo "REFUSED: this is a clean folder; emulator source must never reach it." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

fetch() {
    refuse_in_clean_folder
    work=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    git -C "$work" init -q
    git -C "$work" remote add origin "$UPSTREAM_URL"
    git -C "$work" fetch -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none origin "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    git -C "$work" sparse-checkout set --no-cone $UPSTREAM_PATHS
    git -C "$work" -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
    got=$(git -C "$work" rev-parse HEAD)
    [ "$got" = "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT" ] || { echo "fetched $got, want $UPSTREAM_COMMIT"; exit 1; }
    for p in $(ls "$DEST/patches"/*.patch 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        git -C "$work" apply --whitespace=nowarn "$p"
        echo "applied $(basename "$p")"
    done
    keep=$(mktemp -d)
    for f in $OURS patches; do [ -e "$DEST/$f" ] && cp -R "$DEST/$f" "$keep/"; done
    rm -rf "$DEST"
    mkdir -p "$DEST/crates"
    cp "$work/LICENSE" "$work/Cargo.toml" "$DEST/"
    for c in fm1-isa fm1-core fm1-soc; do cp -R "$work/crates/$c" "$DEST/crates/"; done
    for f in $OURS patches; do [ -e "$keep/$f" ] && cp -R "$keep/$f" "$DEST/"; done
    rm -rf "$keep"
    verify
}

case "${1:---verify}" in
    --verify) verify ;;
    --fetch) fetch ;;
    --sums) sums ;;
    *) echo "usage: $0 [--verify|--fetch|--sums]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Vendors three crates of the public emulator upstream, at a pinned commit,
# into vendor/emulator/, applies the patches in vendor/emulator/patches/, and
# checks every file against vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS, whose own SHA-256 is
# the tree hash below (PROVENANCE P-7). Spec side only: vendor/emulator/ is
# left out of clean folders, and --fetch refuses to run in one.
#
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --verify   check the committed files (default,
#                                      offline; SKIP when vendor/emulator/
#                                      isn't on disk, as in a clean folder)
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --fetch    re-download them from the pinned commit,
#                                      apply the patches, then verify
#
# The fetch is a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout of exactly the paths
# in UPSTREAM_PATHS, so nothing else in that repository reaches the disk.
# To move to another commit: change UPSTREAM_COMMIT, run --fetch in a spec
# folder, rewrite SHA256SUMS (--sums), update TREE_SHA256 and UPSTREAM.md,
# and log it in PROVENANCE.md, all in one pull request.
set -eu

UPSTREAM_URL=https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu.git
UPSTREAM_COMMIT=43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f
UPSTREAM_PATHS="
/LICENSE
/Cargo.toml
/crates/fm1-isa/
/crates/fm1-core/
/crates/fm1-soc/
"
# SHA-256 of vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS: one hash for the whole tree.
TREE_SHA256=0553473ab8b76fe289c0c4c7609ed3ade622a5f4510b185b099cfdcb7bfd4a29

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
DEST="$ROOT/vendor/emulator"
SUMS="$DEST/SHA256SUMS"
# Ours, not upstream's: not listed in SHA256SUMS.
OURS="SHA256SUMS UPSTREAM.md"

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

listed_files() {
    (cd "$DEST" && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort) | while read -r f; do
        case " $OURS " in *" $f "*) continue ;; esac
        printf '%s\n' "$f"
    done
}

verify() {
    if [ ! -d "$DEST" ]; then
        echo "SKIP: vendor/emulator/ is not on disk (a clean folder leaves it out)"
        return 0
    fi
    status=0
    got=$(sha256 "$SUMS")
    if [ "$got" = "$TREE_SHA256" ]; then echo "OK      SHA256SUMS (tree hash $TREE_SHA256)"
    else echo "CHANGED SHA256SUMS ($got, want $TREE_SHA256)"; status=1; fi
    while read -r want path; do
        [ -n "$want" ] || continue
        if [ ! -f "$DEST/$path" ]; then
            echo "MISSING $path"; status=1; continue
        fi
        [ "$(sha256 "$DEST/$path")" = "$want" ] || { echo "CHANGED $path"; status=1; }
    done < "$SUMS"
    for f in $(listed_files); do
        if ! awk -v p="$f" '$2 == p { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$SUMS"; then
            echo "UNLISTED $f"; status=1
        fi
    done
    n=$(grep -c . "$SUMS")
    if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then echo "$n emulator files match commit $UPSTREAM_COMMIT plus patches"; fi
    return $status
}

sums() {
    (cd "$DEST" && for f in $(listed_files); do printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256 "$f")" "$f"; done) > "$SUMS"
    echo "wrote SHA256SUMS: tree hash $(sha256 "$SUMS")"
}

refuse_in_clean_folder() {
    role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$role" = clean ] || git -C "$ROOT" sparse-checkout list 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^!/vendor/emulator/'; then
        echo "REFUSED: this is a clean folder; emulator source must never reach it." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

fetch() {
    refuse_in_clean_folder
    work=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    git -C "$work" init -q
    git -C "$work" remote add origin "$UPSTREAM_URL"
    git -C "$work" fetch -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none origin "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    git -C "$work" sparse-checkout set --no-cone $UPSTREAM_PATHS
    git -C "$work" -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
    got=$(git -C "$work" rev-parse HEAD)
    [ "$got" = "$UPSTREAM_COMMIT" ] || { echo "fetched $got, want $UPSTREAM_COMMIT"; exit 1; }
    for p in $(ls "$DEST/patches"/*.patch 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        git -C "$work" apply --whitespace=nowarn "$p"
        echo "applied $(basename "$p")"
    done
    keep=$(mktemp -d)
    for f in $OURS patches; do [ -e "$DEST/$f" ] && cp -R "$DEST/$f" "$keep/"; done
    rm -rf "$DEST"
    mkdir -p "$DEST/crates"
    cp "$work/LICENSE" "$work/Cargo.toml" "$DEST/"
    for c in fm1-isa fm1-core fm1-soc; do cp -R "$work/crates/$c" "$DEST/crates/"; done
    for f in $OURS patches; do [ -e "$keep/$f" ] && cp -R "$keep/$f" "$DEST/"; done
    rm -rf "$keep"
    verify
}

case "${1:---verify}" in
    --verify) verify ;;
    --fetch) fetch ;;
    --sums) sums ;;
    *) echo "usage: $0 [--verify|--fetch|--sums]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# The harness's CI steps (spec side). tools/record.py runs them as the
# C-HARNESS-* checks, and skips them where harness/ isn't on disk.
#
#   harness/ci.sh tag                print the local image tag
#   harness/ci.sh image              build the runtime image (and print the
#                                    fwtest binary's SHA-256)
#   harness/ci.sh test               build the test stage: cargo test
#   harness/ci.sh suite OUT MOUNT    run tests/harness.suite in a fresh
#                                    container, harness/tests mounted
#                                    read-only at MOUNT; outputs in OUT
#   harness/ci.sh scope              the harness never uses the vendored
#                                    crates' update-package or stock-boot paths
#   harness/ci.sh context            write the build context (a tar) to stdout
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$@"
    else shasum -a 256 "$@"; fi
}

# The image tag: a hash of everything that goes into the build context.
tag() {
    h=$(cd "$ROOT" && context_files | LC_ALL=C sort | while read -r f; do sha256 "$f"; done | sha256 | cut -c1-16)
    echo "small-beeps-fwtest:$h"
}

# (The spec-side experiments are not part of fwtest: harness/spec-experiments/
# runs them against it.)
context_files() {
    git -C "$ROOT" ls-files vendor/emulator harness LICENSE NOTICE | grep -v '^harness/spec-experiments/'
}

# A tar of exactly the tracked context files (its owners and times don't
# matter: the build's outputs don't depend on them).
context() {
    cd "$ROOT"
    context_files | LC_ALL=C sort > "$tmp/files"
    tar --format=ustar -c -f - -T "$tmp/files" 2>/dev/null \
        || tar -c -f - $(cat "$tmp/files")
}

build() {
    target=$1 t=$2
    context | docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" --target "$target" -t "$t" -f harness/Dockerfile -
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

case "${1:-}" in
    tag) tag ;;
    context) context ;;
    image)

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                        [--demo plaits]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds only, tools/perf.py);
#                                             --demo builds a demo's own
#                                             image instead (M4b: the
#                                             Plaits load test), never the
#                                             firmware's
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src defines="" demo=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --define)

    # own already makes the compiler use the instructions.
    CPU="-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1"

    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.

    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -nostdinc -Werror"

# container runs as linux/amd64 with no network, as your user. After a run,
# DIR/runner.txt names the image used, for the record.
#
# FWTEST_IMAGE overrides the pinned image (spec side, to try a local build);
# runner.txt then says the image was not the pinned one.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PIN_FILE="$ROOT/config/fwtest-image"
pinned=$(grep -v '^#' "$PIN_FILE" | grep . | head -1)

if [ -n "${FWTEST_IMAGE:-}" ]; then
    ref=$FWTEST_IMAGE
    note="not the pinned image (FWTEST_IMAGE); pinned: $pinned"
else
    case "$pinned" in

    esac
    ref=$pinned
    note="pinned (config/fwtest-image)"
fi

## Instructions

fwtest runs the code the pinned toolchain's compiler emits for the
firmware's flags (`-target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`, tools/build.sh),
with the known gaps below. That was checked on a corpus, not proven for
every instruction (SR-7). The corpus: the firmware at `18d9459`, the
vendored Plaits and the demo's C++ built with the firmware's CPU flags,
and several hundred small C functions written to vary types, operations
and pointer patterns, each at `-Os` and `-O2`. Two checks ran in fwtest
0.3.0, each unit on its own:

- every distinct disassembled unit of the corpus's objects (13 981; a
  dual-issue pair is one unit; some are constants in the code, decoded
  as if they were instructions);
- every form in the compiler's assembly output (660, registers and numbers
  abstracted), with each register slot set in turn to r0 to r15 (register
  pairs to each even-odd pair) and each number to values from 0 and ±1 up
  to the 32-bit limits, as far as the assembler accepts them: 34 437
  distinct encodings.

They show only that fwtest decodes and runs each one, not that it
computes what the chip does. An instruction neither check held can still
end a run as a fault ("Outcomes and exit codes"): report it as SR-7 was,
with its bytes and the smallest image that shows it.

Known gaps (fwtest 0.3.0). Each ends the run as a fault, "an instruction
the emulated CPU cannot decode":

- **Rotate by a register.** `rD = rS <> rT` (bytes `cc e1`, then two
  bytes naming the registers), for every register. The compiler emits it,
  at `-Os` too, for a rotate by an amount it doesn't know at compile time,
  such as `(x << s) | (x >> (32 - s))`. A rotate by a constant
  (`rD = rS <> n`, bytes `c4 e1`) runs. Until fwtest runs it, keep rotate
  amounts constant, or hide the amount from the compiler (a `volatile`
  shift count, for example).
- **A 4-byte push or pop of a register list whose lowest register is
  above r0.** `[--sp] = {list}` (bytes `d8 e8`, then the 16-bit mask) and
  `{list} = [sp++]` (`d4 e8`, then the mask), without `rets` or `pc`: for
  example `[--sp] = {r5-r1}` or `{r11-r6} = [sp++]`. Lists that start at
  r0 run, and so do the 2-byte forms and the forms with `rets` or `pc`.
  The compiler was not seen to emit the failing lists (an interrupt
  handler saves a list from r0); hand-written assembly can.

### Block moves with a register base

Since 0.3.0 fwtest runs all eight modes of this 4-byte instruction (bytes
`xm eb`, then a 16-bit register mask; HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-66). As the
toolchain's disassembler writes them, with n registers in the list:

| First byte | Form | Words moved | The base after |
|------------|------|-------------|----------------|
| `0x0N` | `{list} = [rN+]` | rN to rN + 4n - 4 | unchanged |
| `0x1N` | `{list} = [rN++]` | rN to rN + 4n - 4 | rN + 4n |
| `0x2N` | `[rN+] = {list}` | rN to rN + 4n - 4 | unchanged |
| `0x3N` | `[rN++] = {list}` | rN to rN + 4n - 4 | rN + 4n |
| `0x4N` | `{list} = [-rN]` | rN - 4n to rN - 4 | unchanged |
| `0x5N` | `{list} = [--rN]` | rN - 4n to rN - 4 | rN - 4n |
| `0x6N` | `[-rN] = {list}` | rN - 4n to rN - 4 | unchanged |
| `0x7N` | `[--rN] = {list}` | rN - 4n to rN - 4 | rN - 4n |

- The lowest-numbered register in the list takes the lowest address.
- Every address comes from the base as it was before the instruction. A
  base that is also in a loaded list, in a mode without `++` / `--`, ends
  with its loaded word (the compiler relies on this); in a write-back mode
  it ends with the written-back address. A store writes the base's
  value from before the instruction.
- An empty list moves nothing (and a write-back mode leaves the base as
  it was).
- The compiler emits the modes without `++` / `--` (`0x0`, `0x2`, `0x4`,
  `0x6`). The write-back modes, a write-back mode whose base is in its
  list, and an empty list are not established for the chip (Q-19): avoid
  relying on them.

Before 0.3.0 the four modes below the base (`0x4` to `0x7`) ended the run
as a fault, "an instruction the emulator does not implement".

input.command:
S=/tmp/claude-UID/-HOME-Development-[REDACTED:private]-spec/9d5d3a07-eba7-4567-8198-f0382f4ba9b0/scratchpad; cd $S/emu && git log --oneline; P=~/Development/[REDACTED:private]/spec/vendor/emulator/patches; 
hdr() { cat; }
{ cat <<'EOF'
A dual-issue pair's head among the 4-byte ALU forms no table class fits
(byte 1 f0 / f1, the twins of e0 / e1 that the fallback decoder reads)
ran unpaired: its result was written at once, so the pair's second half
saw the new value, not the old. Such words now decode as a pair head
(an entry whose syntax ends in `#`); the e0 / e1 words decode as before.

The F-Emulator app's patch (its 0003, emulator-patches.md section A),
taken unchanged: the added and removed lines are the app's, byte for
byte, with only the line offsets refreshed for our 0003. Licensed MIT
for this repository by the owner (PROVENANCE P-37).

Behaviour from the vendor toolchain: its objdump prints every f0 / f1
twin of these families with the trailing `#` that marks a pair's head,
and the vendor compiler's own code relies on a pair's second half
seeing the registers as they were before the head (our firmware's
input.c at -O2: `r1 = 0x50000 #` paired with `b[r1+9] = r2`, a
read-modify-write of the byte it had just loaded from [r1+9]).

The app's crate test alu4_fallback_keeps_pair_head comes with it; the
harness test alu_pair_heads_hold_their_result (every family, image
tests/images/pairhead.S) fails without it. Session emulator-parity,
2026-10-24.

EOF
git diff ff2fa85~1 ff2fa85; } > $P/0004-pair-heads-without-a-table-class.patch
{ cat <<'EOF'
The rotate right by a register, `rD = rS <> rT` (cc e1 S0 DT, and cc f1,
a dual-issue pair's head), had no decoder: no table class, so every
register combination ended the run as an instruction the emulated CPU
cannot decode. The vendor compiler emits it for any rotate by a
variable amount: `(x << s) | (x >> (32 - s))` is `r1 = 0x20 - r1;
r0 = r0 <> r1`.

Fields from the vendor assembler and objdump: d bits 28-31, s bits
20-23, t bits 24-27, the `c8 e1` register shifts' layout; byte 2's low
nibble 0 is `<>`, 1 to 3 are `<c>`, `><` and `>< (sat)` (not taken
here), 4 to f no instruction. Behaviour from the compiler's code: it
rotates right (`(x >> 7) | (x << 25)` is `<> 7`, and the idiom above
rotates left by s through `<> (32 - s)`), and by 0 it leaves the value
(the masked idiom `(x << (s & 31)) | (x >> (-s & 31))` is `r1 = 0x0 -
r1; r1 = r1 & 0x1F; r0 = r0 <> r1`). An amount of 32 or more: taken
mod 32, by analogy (a rotate repeats every 32; the compiler masks such
amounts itself).

Decoded from the raw bits beside the rotate by a constant; executed on
the slow path, as that one is. The harness tests rotate_by_a_register
(tests/images/rotr.S) and rotates_from_the_compiler (rotc.c, built with
the firmware's CPU flags) fail without it. Session emulator-parity,
2026-10-24.

EOF
git diff 36f47f0~1 36f47f0; } > $P/0005-rotate-by-a-register.patch
{ cat <<'EOF'
The 4-byte push and pop of a register list without rets or pc,
`[--sp] = {list}` (d8 e8 <mask>) and `{list} = [sp++]` (d4 e8 <mask>),
decoded only for the masks the table's classes fit, lists from r0:
`[--sp] = {r5-r1}`, `{r11-r6} = [sp++]` or `{r15} = [sp++]` ended the
run as an instruction the emulated CPU cannot decode. A raw decoder now
takes every mask, as the ones for the forms with rets or pc do, and the
executor the table's entries already use runs it (the mask from the
raw word).

Encoding from the vendor assembler and objdump: mask bit k is rk, every
mask is an instruction (`{}` too). Behaviour: the same as the lists
from r0 the compiler emits in interrupt handlers (`[--sp] = {r1, r0}`,
`{r7-r0} = [sp++]`): sp moves by 4 a register, the lowest register at
the lowest address. The compiler was not seen to emit a list above r0,
so that is by analogy.

The harness test push_pop_any_register_list (tests/images/pushpop.S)
fails without it. Session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24.

EOF
git diff fa0b44f~1 fa0b44f; } > $P/0006-push-pop-any-register-list.patch
{ cat <<'EOF'
Speed only: the peripherals' addresses, all below 16 MB but the
interrupt controller's, are looked up before the memories are tried.
No address reaches anything different.

The F-Emulator app's patch (its 0004, emulator-patches.md section C),
taken unchanged: the added and removed lines are the app's, byte for
byte. Licensed MIT for this repository by the owner (PROVENANCE P-37).

Its crate test region_is_what_it_was compares the new lookup with the
old one (copied into the test exactly as it is at our base, whitespace
aside) at every address below 0x04200000, the memories' included, and
a sweep above, for both boards and both XIP-flash settings. fwtest's
outputs are byte for byte the same with and without this patch and
0008 (docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md). Session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24.

EOF
git diff b78db23~1 b78db23; } > $P/0007-peripherals-before-memories.patch
{ cat <<'EOF'
Speed only: a block built from RAM code is found current by the bus's
count of writes to code words, when the count hasn't changed, before
its bytes are compared with memory; upstream did so only in its wasm
build. Every write to a word a RAM block was built from is counted:
RAM's bytes are reachable only through its write methods, which count,
and the native JITs' inline stores, which send a store to a flagged word
to the bus; a block marks exactly the bytes it keeps as code. fwtest
runs without the JIT.

The F-Emulator app's patch (its 0005, emulator-patches.md section D),
taken unchanged: the added and removed lines are the app's, byte for
byte. Licensed MIT for this repository by the owner (PROVENANCE P-37).

Its crate test ram_block_sees_patched_code re-enters a RAM block after a
store patched it, interpreted and with the JIT. fwtest's outputs are
byte for byte the same with and without this patch and 0007
(docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md). Session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24.

EOF
git diff ce2154f~1 ce2154f; } > $P/0008-ram-blocks-by-write-count.patch
ls -la $P; grep -c "" $P/*.patch

cwd=$(pwd -P)
inside() {
    # a path argument as the container sees it, or an error if it is outside cwd
    case "$1" in

        *) p="$cwd/$1" ;;
    esac
    d=$(dirname "$p")
    if [ -d "$d" ]; then p="$(cd "$d" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$p")"; fi
    case "$p" in

# Spec-side black-box experiments (spec side only)

Small images the spec side runs in fwtest to confirm facts in
`docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (M0c). The spec cites them only as E-n and their
result; nothing here leaves `harness/`. They are written from the JieLi
SDK's register map and, where the SDK has no bit meanings, from the vendored
emulator's model (`exp.h` says which). Each confirms how fwtest presents the
board, not how real hardware behaves.

- Build: `sh harness/spec-experiments/build.sh` (the pinned toolchain
  container; writes `images/` and `images/SHA256SUMS`).
- Run: `sh harness/spec-experiments/run.sh OUT` rebuilds, compares with the
  committed images, and runs `experiments.suite` against this checkout's
  fwtest (C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS, R-SPEC-4). The golden files are the results.
- Not part of fwtest: `harness/ci.sh` leaves this folder out of the fwtest
  build context, and the image-publishing workflow ignores it.

| ID | Image | What it shows (the golden files hold the numbers) |
|----|-------|---------------------------------------------------|
| E-1 | `e1-boot` | At entry: r0 = 0x01C7FC00, r2..r15, sp, usp, ssp, icfg, psr and cnum all 0 (r1 not observable: used as the pointer). The block at r0: first word 0x01C7FC40, the other 15 zero. The code window past the image reads 0xFFFFFFFF (erased flash), also 4 KiB further. A written word reads back at 0x01C7FDFC, 0x01CFFFFC, 0x01F3FFFC and 0x0407FFFC. |
| E-2 | `e2-console` | Word writes to DBG_MSG append their 4 bytes, low byte first. A byte or halfword write appends 4 bytes too: the written bytes merged into the last word written (console "abcd12:\nX2:\nYZ:\nend\n"). |
| E-3 | `e3-timers` | TIMER5 PRD 600: an interrupt (63) every 100 µs; TIMER4 advanced 2400 counts (24 MHz) between two. TIMER0 prescaler index 2, PRD 1500: an interrupt (4) every 1 ms; its CON read in the handler is 0x8021 (bit 15 pending). TTMR with PRD 1234: an interrupt (3) every 10 ms. ILAT_SET bit 0: interrupt 120 once. Counts at 52.3 ms (the capture came late, below): 523, 52, 5, 1. |
| E-4 | `e4-core1` | With core 1's entry in the word at 0x01C7FFF8, setting C1_CON bit 3 starts core 1 there; cnum reads 0 on core 0 and 1 on core 1; core 1 ran on stacks it set itself. |
| E-5 | `e5-lcd` | SPI1 bytes with PC8 low are commands, high data. CASET/RASET/RAMWR with RGB565 pixels high byte first, by single bytes (BUF) and by DMA (ADR, CNT from RAM) both draw. INVON and DISPOFF leave the captured picture as written. A software reset (0x01) clears it to black. |
| E-6 | `e6-matrix` | The log gives each fwtest key's (column, row) and each encoder's two contacts and their order (clockwise: the second contact closes first). Matches the table in the spec. |
| E-7 | `e7-leds` | LED line PA9, PA10, PH6, PH9 lights, in the selected column, the LED of the key at row 1, 2, 3, 4 of that column. |
| E-8 | `e8-adc` | Channel 4 reads the pot (900 at the start, then the script's 300, 0, 1023); channel 3 reads 640; every other channel 512. |
| E-9 | `e9-audio` | A half of 128 words (64 frames) every 1.451 ms after the first at 1.459 ms (44 117.6 frames a second). The first half to finish is half 0; the half just finished is CON0 bit 15 inverted. A sample is the word shifted right by 8, clamped to 16 bits: 0x007fffff gives 32767, 0xff800000 -32768, 0x01000000 32767, 0x00000080 0. |
| E-10 | `e10-faults` | No fault reaches sources 0-2 (handlers count 0), before and after writing EMU_CON 0x001F010F, EMU_SSP/USP limits excluding the stacks, DBG_EN 0x003F0030. Misaligned word loads give the bytes at the address (RAM+1: 0x04030201; code+1: 0x14131211); halfword loads at RAM+1 and +3 give 0x0100 and 0x0302 (the lowest address bit ignored); a word stored at RAM+9 lands in bytes 9-12. The addresses come from a volatile word: with constant addresses the compiler split the RAM accesses into byte accesses. Unmapped 0x00ABCDEC reads 0, and after a write still 0. A code-window write reads back unchanged. Signed and unsigned 1234/0 give 0; 1234%0 (as compiled) gives 1234. EMU_CON and the limits read back; EMU_MSG 0; DBG_EN 0 (unmodelled). The console is "E10\nend\n": writes to DBG_WR_EN and DBG_MSG_CLR between the two words left it alone. |
| E-11 | `e11-undefined` | A call to a function whose first halfword is 0xFFFF: the run ends as a fault ("cannot decode"), after the marker, with no handler run. |
| E-12 | `e12-badjump` | A call to 0x00ABCDEE: fwtest runs the zeros it reads there for 1024 instructions, then ends the run as a fault ("the pc left every memory"); no handler ran. |
| E-13 | `e13-timer-ack` | TIMER0, prescaler index 2, PRD 1500: 100 periods are 2 400 100 TIMER4 ticks with the acknowledge first in the handler (1 tick after entry) and 2 408 160 with it 82 ticks after entry; CNT reads 5 just before the acknowledge, 0 just after. The periphery model restarts the count and the period at every CON write. |
| E-14 | `e14-undefined-inline` | A marker store, then the halfword 0xFFFF in the same straight-line code: the run ends as a fault at the start of that code (the pc of main's first instruction), and the marker was never written. |
| E-15 | `e15-spi1-irq` | SPI1 CON bit 13 and source 16. CON reads 0x8000 before any write. Bit 13 never set, or written clear: no interrupt for a 2-byte DMA or a BUF byte. Bit 13 set: one interrupt each (the handler acknowledges with `CON |= 0x4000`); CON reads 0xA000. A DMA done with bit 13 set and the source off in ICFG, then CON written 0 and the source turned on: taken once. Before the SR-3 fix (vendor patch 0002, fwtest 0.2.0) a CON write could not clear bit 13, so the clear steps counted too. |
| E-16 | `e16-lcd-frame` | One CNT write of 115 200 bytes from RAM draws a whole frame (rows 0-119 red, 120-239 blue), pixel (0,0) green and (239,239) white in place. |

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

Push/pop above r0 is by analogy with the lists from r0 the compiler emits.

# Upstream report: the block moves below a base register don't run

For the owner to file with `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` and to apply in the
F-Emulator app. Spec side only; not filed by a session. Found in session
SR-7 (2026-10-24) against commit `43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`;

The block moves with a register base are one 4-byte family, `xm eb
<mask>` with m < 8: the base register in bits 0-3, a 16-bit register mask
(bit k: rk) in bits 16-31, and three mode bits in bits 4-6 (4: write the
base back, 5: store, 6: the block lies below the base). The vendor
toolchain's disassembler names the eight modes:

|-------|------|

| `1N eb` | `{list} = [rN++]` |
| `2N eb` | `[rN+] = {list}` |
| `3N eb` | `[rN++] = {list}` |
| `4N eb` | `{list} = [-rN]` |
| `5N eb` | `{list} = [--rN]` |
| `6N eb` | `[-rN] = {list}` |

  show (it masks such amounts itself): don't rely on it.

  (`d4 e8`, then the mask), without `rets` or `pc`: every list, for
  example `[--sp] = {r5-r1}`, `{r11-r6} = [sp++]` or `{r15} = [sp++]`, as

  same way. The compiler emits only lists from r0 (in interrupt
  handlers); lists above r0 behave the same by analogy, not checked
  against the chip.

  stores a byte back through the base register the head changes). Until
  0.3.0 a few of the 4-byte ALU forms as a pair's head (for example
  `rD = rA ^ (1 << rB) #`, `rD = rA << rB #`, `rD = rA * rB #`) wrote
  their result at once, so the second half saw the new value.

firmware's flags (`-target pi32v2 -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`, tools/build.sh),
with the known gaps below. That was checked on a corpus, not proven for
every instruction (SR-7). The corpus: the firmware at `18d9459`, the
vendored Plaits and the demo's C++ built with the firmware's CPU flags,
and several hundred small C functions written to vary types, operations
and pointer patterns, each at `-Os` and `-O2`. Two checks ran in fwtest
0.3.0, each unit on its own:

- every distinct disassembled unit of the corpus's objects (13 981; a
  dual-issue pair is one unit; some are constants in the code, decoded
  as if they were instructions);

  abstracted), with each register slot set in turn to r0 to r15 (register
  pairs to each even-odd pair) and each number to values from 0 and ±1 up

  distinct encodings.

with its bytes and the smallest image that shows it.

# Emulator parity: fwtest and the F-Emulator app

fwtest (this repository's harness) and the owner's F-Emulator app both run
the public emulator upstream, `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`, with patches of
their own. This file lists every patch and which of the two has it, so
that a firmware behaves the same in both. Written by the spec side

# For the F-Emulator app: the patches it doesn't have yet

For the owner, to apply in the app (and, where marked, to file upstream).
Spec side only. Session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24, against the app's
patch notes as the owner dropped them (PROVENANCE P-37) and upstream
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`. docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md has
the whole table.

## What to apply

Three of fwtest's patches, in this order, on the app's tree (upstream, its
fwtest-0001/0002 base, its 0003 to 0006):

| fwtest patch | What | Upstream report |
|--------------|------|-----------------|
| `vendor/emulator/patches/0003-block-moves-below-the-base.patch` | The block moves with a register base, all eight modes (SR-7) | `fm1-emu-block-moves.md` |
| `vendor/emulator/patches/0005-rotate-by-a-register.patch` | `rD = rS <> rT` (`cc e1` / `cc f1`) | `fm1-emu-undecoded-forms.md` |
| `vendor/emulator/patches/0006-push-pop-any-register-list.patch` | `d8 e8` / `d4 e8` with any mask | `fm1-emu-undecoded-forms.md` |

Checked in this session on a copy: upstream with fwtest's 0001 and 0002,
then the app's 0003, 0004, 0005 and 0006 (as dropped), then these three
with `git apply`. Every hunk applies, none needs its context refreshed,
only line offsets move (0003: -1 to +25 lines; 0005 and 0006: -1). The
crates' own tests pass after (73: 44, 7 and 22). `crates/fm1-core` is then
byte for byte fwtest 0.4.0's; `crates/fm1-soc` differs only by the app's
raw-image loader (its 0006), 61 added lines.

The app's notes say SR-7's form "faults" in fwtest and that the two
patches meet only in `decode_any`: true of fwtest 0.2.0. fwtest 0.3.0's
0003 decodes the `xm eb` block moves in `exec_syntax` and `fast_of`, not
in `decode_any`, so it and the app's pair-head fix touch different
functions.

## Already the app's, now fwtest's too

The app's 0003 (A, the pair heads), 0004 (C) and 0005 (D) are fwtest's
0004, 0007 and 0008, with the same added and removed lines. A's upstream
report is the app's own (its notes' "Upstream bug reports", 1); file that
one. fwtest's harness test `alu_pair_heads_hold_their_result` (image
`harness/tests/images/pairhead.S`, one word of each fallback family, plain
and as a pair head) can go with it: in 0.3.0's emulator two of its 25
cases saw the new value (`94 f1 51 63` and `c8 f1 53 63`), so which words
reach the fallback depends on the registers, not only the family.

## Two things in the drop to look at

- The app's `0006-raw-image-boot.patch` inserts `RAW_IMAGE_MAX`,
  `RawImage`, `raw_image` and `raw_boot` inside fm1-soc's `mod tests`,
  after its `use super::*;`, so they compile only in test builds and are
  not part of the crate's API. The app's own branch may differ from the
  file dropped; fwtest doesn't use the patch either way.
- The notes give the reproduction for A as a fwtest command line not yet
  run on fwtest. It now is, as part of the harness test above.
