# For the F-Emulator app: the patches it doesn't have yet

For the owner, to apply in the app (and, where marked, to file upstream).
Spec side only. Session emulator-parity, 2026-10-24, against the app's
patch notes as the owner dropped them (PROVENANCE P-37) and upstream
`43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f`. docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md has
the whole table.

## What to apply

Three of fwtest's patches, in this order, on the app's tree (upstream, its
fwtest-0001/0002 base, its 0003 to 0006):

| fwtest patch | What | Upstream report |
|--------------|------|-----------------|
| `vendor/emulator/patches/0003-block-moves-below-the-base.patch` | The block moves with a register base, all eight modes (SR-7) | `fm1-emu-block-moves.md` |
| `vendor/emulator/patches/0005-rotate-by-a-register.patch` | `rD = rS <> rT` (`cc e1` / `cc f1`) | `fm1-emu-undecoded-forms.md` |
| `vendor/emulator/patches/0006-push-pop-any-register-list.patch` | `d8 e8` / `d4 e8` with any mask | `fm1-emu-undecoded-forms.md` |

Checked in this session on a copy: upstream with fwtest's 0001 and 0002,
then the app's 0003, 0004, 0005 and 0006 (as dropped), then these three
with `git apply`. Every hunk applies, none needs its context refreshed,
only line offsets move (0003: -1 to +25 lines; 0005 and 0006: -1). The
crates' own tests pass after (73: 44, 7 and 22). `crates/fm1-core` is then
byte for byte fwtest 0.4.0's; `crates/fm1-soc` differs only by the app's
raw-image loader (its 0006), 61 added lines.

The app's notes say SR-7's form "faults" in fwtest and that the two
patches meet only in `decode_any`: true of fwtest 0.2.0. fwtest 0.3.0's
0003 decodes the `xm eb` block moves in `exec_syntax` and `fast_of`, not
in `decode_any`, so it and the app's pair-head fix touch different
functions.

## Already the app's, now fwtest's too

The app's 0003 (A, the pair heads), 0004 (C) and 0005 (D) are fwtest's
0004, 0007 and 0008, with the same added and removed lines. A's upstream
report is the app's own (its notes' "Upstream bug reports", 1); file that
one. fwtest's harness test `alu_pair_heads_hold_their_result` (image
`harness/tests/images/pairhead.S`, one word of each fallback family, plain
and as a pair head) can go with it: in 0.3.0's emulator two of its 25
cases saw the new value (`94 f1 51 63` and `c8 f1 53 63`), so which words
reach the fallback depends on the registers, not only the family.

## Two things in the drop to look at

- The app's `0006-raw-image-boot.patch` inserts `RAW_IMAGE_MAX`,
  `RawImage`, `raw_image` and `raw_boot` inside fm1-soc's `mod tests`,
  after its `use super::*;`, so they compile only in test builds and are
  not part of the crate's API. The app's own branch may differ from the
  file dropped; fwtest doesn't use the patch either way.
- The notes give the reproduction for A as a fwtest command line not yet
  run on fwtest. It now is, as part of the harness test above.

  fwtest: exit 3, `fault`, "core 0 at pc 0x02000016: an instruction the
  emulator does not implement", nothing stored. The control image, the
  same with `r4 += -8; r0 = [r4+0]; r3 = [r4+4]` in place of the one
  instruction: exit 4, `halt` as meant, and the stores show r0
  `0x29F3A1C5`, r3 `0x7E41D60B`, r4 `0x01C00008`, which is what we expect
  the one instruction to leave (which register gets which word is part of
  the question).
- Workaround until then: `voice_start()` copies those fields a word at a
  time through a volatile pointer (`copy_words`, fm_play.c), and
  tools/build.sh fails an image whose disassembly holds the form, so
  none reaches fwtest unnoticed (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M5). Both go once
  fwtest runs it.
- Status: answered (HARDWARE-SPEC.md, "15. Block moves with a register
  base (SR-7)", HW-66; docs/HARNESS.md, "Instructions"): the encoding has
  eight modes, loads and stores, up or below the base, with or without
  moving it, for any base and any list of r0 to r15; fwtest 0.3.0 runs all
  eight. The lowest register takes the lowest address, so your r0 and r3
  are right, but the form without `--` leaves the base as it was: r4 stays
  `0x01C00010`, not `0x01C00008` (the compiler's own code relies on this).
  The compiler emits the forms without `++` / `--`; the others, and a base
  that is also in a write-back form's list, are open for the chip (Q-19).
  A corpus check of what the compiler emits for the firmware's flags,
  across registers and immediates, found two more forms fwtest doesn't
  run: a rotate by a register, which the compiler emits, and a 4-byte push
  or pop of a list not starting at r0, which it was not seen to emit
  (HARNESS.md, "Instructions", "Known gaps").
  fwtest 0.3.0 reaches `tools/fwtest` when the pull request after this
  one pins its image; then `copy_words` and build.sh's check can go.
- Answered: 2026-10-24, session SR-7 (spec side)

**What:** fwtest 0.4.0. The vendored emulator gains five patches (0004 to 0008):
- **0004:** the F-Emulator app's pair-head fix. A dual-issue pair's head among the 4-byte ALU forms keeps its result until after the pair.
- **0005:** the rotate right by a register now runs.
- **0006:** the 4-byte push and pop of any register list now run.
- **0007 and 0008:** the app's two speed-only changes.

Each new behaviour has a harness test image built by the pinned toolchain. `docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md` lists the upstream commit and every patch, with whether fwtest and the app each have it. `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-app-parity.md` says what the app still needs to apply: our 0003, 0005 and 0006.

**Why:** emulator-parity: fwtest and the app should run the same emulator. 0005 and 0006 close the two gaps SR-7's sweep found (R-HARN-12).

**How:**
- **The app's patches** (owner-licensed MIT, P-37) are taken unchanged: their added and removed lines match the app's line for line.
- **Behaviour comes from the vendor toolchain** (P-38):
  - its disassembler on both twins of every form;
  - our firmware's own compiled pairs;
  - the compiler's rotate idioms, one image built with the firmware's flags.
- **Speed-only patches went in only after three checks:**
  - the app's equivalence test for the address lookup;
  - an audit of every way RAM is written;
  - byte-identical outputs with and without them.
- **The app's raw-image loader is not taken:** fwtest has its own.

**Result:**
- **Harness tests:** all 32 pass. Without 0004, 0005 or 0006, only that patch's own tests fail. The RAM-code test passes with and without 0007 and 0008.
- **Crate tests:** the vendored crates' own tests pass after every patch.
- **Same outputs:** the firmware suite (at `cdfd067`), the spec experiments and the harness suite were run on fwtest built three ways: 0.3.0's emulator, with 0004 to 0006, and with all five. All 284 output files are byte-for-byte identical across the three builds. So no firmware result changes, and 0007 and 0008 change nothing.
- **The app's tree:** our three patches apply to the app's patches as dropped with line offsets only, and its crate tests pass.
- **Local record:** every check passes except two that only fail locally. `reuse` isn't installed here, and the logs carry this machine's paths.
- **Speed:** CI's perf summary is what counts here.

Work is done up to the merge. CI passes on PR #77 and it can merge. The next step, publish then pin, needs you.

**Please merge #77** with the "Create a merge commit" button: https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps/pull/77

**What's in it (fwtest 0.4.0):**
- **0004, the app's pair-head fix.** Its code lines are byte-for-byte the app's. Its test fails without it.
- **0005 and 0006, the two gaps SR-7 found.** The rotate by a register and the push/pop of any register list now run. Each has a test that fails without its patch.
- **0007 and 0008, the app's speed-only changes.** I took them because outputs are byte-for-byte identical with and without them.
- **The app's raw-image boot is not taken.** fwtest has its own, as you said; the parity table notes it.
- **Docs:** `docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md` has the upstream commit and every patch, with whether fwtest and the app each have it. `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-app-parity.md` says what the app still needs to apply: our 0003, 0005 and 0006. All three apply to the app's patches as dropped with line offsets only, and its crate tests pass.
- **Firmware:** no change. The firmware suite passes on the pinned 0.3.0 image. Its outputs are byte-for-byte identical on the 0.3.0 emulator and the 0.4.0 one, for the firmware at `cdfd067` and again after #75.

**Things you should know:**
- **ID clash:** the firmware side's #75 took provenance IDs P-37 and P-38, so mine are now P-39 and P-40. The first commits' Sources fields still say P-37 and P-38; the merge commit explains this.
- **Firmware-side guard:** #75 added a check to `tools/build.sh` that fails any image holding a rotate by a register. Its message points at HARNESS.md's "Known gaps" section, which #77 removes. The firmware side can drop that check after the pin; the PR's "Next" says so.
- **The app's 0006:** as dropped, it puts its raw-image functions inside the crate's test module, so they only exist in test builds. Worth checking on the app's branch.
- **Exposure:** the app's notes name community firmwares and quote a two-instruction fragment of one. That's recorded in EXPOSURE.md. The fragment is used only as a bug report; nothing from it appears outside `harness/` and `vendor/emulator/`.
- **SR-8:** a new spec request (MIDI input) arrived on main in #76. It isn't part of this task.

**Still to do after you merge:** I'll take the published digest, open the pin PR, and run the firmware suite on the new image against the 0.3.0 baseline. "Done, ready to clear" comes after that.

**Merge order:** #77 first, then wait for the fwtest-image workflow to publish 0.4.0, then the pin PR.

content.text:
Done, ready to clear.

fwtest 0.4.0 is pinned (#78), so the firmware side now runs the same emulator as the F-Emulator app, except for the app's own raw-image loader.

**What changed:**
- **The app's patches:** its pair-head fix is our 0004, and its two speed-only changes are 0007 and 0008. Their code lines are byte-for-byte the app's.
- **SR-7's two gaps are fixed:** 0005 runs the rotate by a register, and 0006 runs the push/pop of any register list.
- **Tests:** each fix has a harness test that fails without its patch. I took the speed-only changes because outputs are byte-for-byte identical with and without them. The app's raw-image boot isn't taken; the parity table notes it.
- **Docs:** `docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md` lists the upstream commit and every patch, with whether each side has it. `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-app-parity.md` says what the app still needs: our 0003, 0005 and 0006, which apply to its dropped patches with line offsets only.

**Firmware suite on the pinned image: no change.** It passes on 0.4.0. Every output matches the same build on 0.3.0, except the version field each `result.json` records and `runner.txt`. The native comparisons, on firmware before and after #75, also showed no differences.

**For you to look at:**
- **The audit workflow has failed on every merge since #75**, mine included. The audit itself passes (no file pairs above the threshold). The failing step is its self-test, where C-AUDIT-TEXT reports "3 of our files not scorable". This started with #75, so it's likely the firmware side's change, not this work.
- **The firmware side can now drop `tools/build.sh`'s rotate check** (added in #75). Its message still points at HARNESS.md's "Known gaps", which no longer exists.
- **Provenance IDs:** #75 took P-37 and P-38, so mine are P-39 and P-40. The first commits of #77 still say P-37 and P-38 in their Sources fields; the merge commit explains this.
- **The app's dropped 0006** puts its raw-image functions inside the crate's test module, so they only exist in test builds. Worth checking on its real branch.
- **SR-8** (MIDI input) is waiting on main for a spec session.
- **Disk:** 3.9 GB free.

**Merge order:** #77 (merged), then the fwtest-image workflow published 0.4.0, then #78 (merged).
